chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, and Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, all together from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who appoints a man to handle the matter of his wife, so he said, 'Bear witness that I have appointed So-and-so to handle the matter of So-and-so woman,' and he (the representative) divorces her. Is that permissible for the man?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Is a man's divorce valid if he appoints a representative to divorce his wife on his behalf?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal validity of a man appointing a representative (wakil) to effectuate a divorce on his behalf, confirming that the act is permissible (ja'iz) provided the appointment is clear. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding agency (niyabah) in marital dissolution, allowing the husband to delegate the physical act of pronouncement while retaining the legal authority. This ruling underscores the principle that the essence of divorce lies in the husband's intent and declaration, which can be executed through a trusted agent.
